removability.rationale: Deleting Abilities is delete-the-directory plus mechanical, grep-complete deletions (query wrapper, server function, view-model type, the Pokémon page section that links to it) with no dead code left behind. That is as clean as this feature can be removed given the spec's cross-links.

evidence: app/src/lib/server/pokeapi.ts:114, :185, :341 — the sprite URL is constructed in three separate functions (card(), homeList(), teamDetails()); a Deoxys-style sprite fix must land in all three because homeList/teamDetails bypass the card() helper
app/src/lib/server/pokeapi.ts:152-167 vs :321-334 — the 'types of each default Pokémon' map is built twice, verbatim, so a change to that semantics is a two-site fix
app/src/components/PokemonCards.tsx:12 — good news for the sprite bug: rendering reads card.sprite, so all five card lists share one component and no UI file changes
app/src/lib/server/pokeapi.ts:19-56 — by contrast, API base URL and cache policy are single-site (apiBase(), TTL_MS, api()), so those fixes are one obvious place
app/src/routes/index.tsx:7 and app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:62 — URL-param 'first value' parsing is written twice, so a param-handling fix touches two route files
changeability.rationale: Route-level and data-source fixes land in one obvious place, but card construction logic is duplicated three ways inside the server module, so the most likely class of bug (card/sprite/species-mapping) needs N edits in one file — findable, but the codebase itself created the N.

evidence: app/src/lib/queries.ts:1-56 — the only client-facing data surface; every route imports from ~/lib/queries and nothing outside lib/server imports pokeapi.ts, giving a hard server/client seam
app/src/lib/types.ts:3-10, 19-78 — components consume small typed view models (Card, Named, MoveDetail…) rather than raw API payloads, so PokeAPI shape changes are absorbed in one module
app/src/lib/team-store.tsx:7-14 — team state is an explicit context store with a narrow documented interface (team/has/full/add/remove)
app/src/lib/team.ts:43-50 — server-side cookie read (getRequestEvent) and client cookie read coexist in one shared module, guarded by isServer; acceptable but a slightly mixed client/server file
app/src/components/PokemonCards.tsx:17, 30-34 — the generic card list grew a team-specific onRemove prop and 'Remove X' button markup, so one feature's detail lives inside a shared component
coupling.rationale: Layering is genuinely clean: routes → query wrappers → server module, with typed view models at the boundary, which is exactly what makes this code easy to reason about. The two blemishes are the team feature's optional remove-button leaking into PokemonCards and the mixed client/server cookie module.

evidence: app/src/lib/server/pokeapi.ts:118-130 — cardsFor(refs, extra) captures the real variation across move/ability/type card lists (abilities add a hidden flag) without flag-parameter creep; a new Items page wanting cards reuses it as-is

app/src/components/MoveTable.tsx:10-16, 26-28 — config-driven columns plus one justified boolean (showLevel, the only table that genuinely differs) made the spec's sortable-table requirements trivial to add; app/src/components/Section.tsx:6-14 and TypeLink/TypeBadge are small and single-purpose

app/src/routes/moves/[name].tsx:14-24, app/src/routes/abilities/[name].tsx:12-22, app/src/routes/types/[name].tsx:14-24, app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].tsx:159-169 — the preload + createAsync + Switch/Match(NotFound) scaffolding is copy-pasted across four detail routes; an Items section becomes the fifth copy

app/src/lib/server/pokeapi.ts:112-115 — card() exists as the right abstraction but homeList (:185) and teamDetails (:341) re-inline its fields instead of calling it, showing the seam didn't stretch when teamDetails was added

app/src/lib/types.ts:3-10 — Card's optional types/hidden fields mean every consumer branches on shape; a sortBy capability would need either a component flag (breaks team's insertion order) or edits to the three server builders
abstraction_design.rationale: The load-bearing abstractions (query layer, cardsFor, MoveTable, Section) are designed around real variation and stretch well to new resources; the residue is repeated route-page scaffolding and two server functions that duplicated existing helpers instead of reusing them — copy-paste that is shallow and localized rather than structural.

findings.issue: teamDetails duplicates the 'types per default Pokémon' map that homeList already builds at :152-167; the two will drift on any semantics change (e.g. slot handling, form exclusion).
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared async helper (e.g. typesByPokemonId()) next to allTypes() and use it in both homeList and teamDetails.

findings.issue: The sprite URL template is hand-built in three functions (card():114, homeList():185, teamDetails():341) instead of going through the existing card() helper, so a sprite-source fix or change to the /media/ layout is a three-site edit.
findings.suggestion: Add a spriteUrl(id) helper (or make homeList/teamDetails build cards via card()) so the URL exists in exactly one place.

findings.issue: The detail-page scaffolding (route.preload, createAsync, Switch/Match null → NotFound, Title + h1 + facts dl) is repeated nearly identically in moves, abilities, types and pokemon routes; adding Items means a fifth copy.
findings.suggestion: Extract a small shared component or helper (e.g. <DetailPage query={...} key={...}>{(data) => …}</DetailPage>) that owns the null-check/NotFound and Title boilerplate.

findings.issue: The generic card list now contains a team-specific optional onRemove prop, 'Remove <name>' button and card__remove styles, coupling the shared component to one feature's UI.
findings.suggestion: Keep PokemonCards purely presentational and let the team page supply per-item actions via a render-prop/slot, or compose the remove button in the team route's own list.

findings.issue: Array-vs-string search-param handling is re-implemented here while an equivalent first() helper exists locally in routes/index.tsx:7; neither is shared.
findings.suggestion: Move first() into ~/lib/format (or a small ~/lib/params module) and use it in both routes.

findings.issue: The preload duplicates the component's filter-param parsing (q/type/generation/page read twice, in two different ways: URLSearchParams vs useSearchParams).
findings.suggestion: Share one parseFilters(search) function between the preload and the component so the query-string contract lives in one place.

findings.issue: Card mixes three list variants into one type via optional fields (types, hidden), so consumers branch on shape and a future 'sorted' or 'with sprite variant' capability would add more flags.
findings.suggestion: Keep Card as the common core and model list-specific extras via a small generic parameter or per-page list types that extend Card.

findings.issue: The damage-multiplier coverage logic is inlined in teamDetails; any future type-effectiveness UI (e.g. on type pages) would copy it.
findings.suggestion: Extract a damageMultiplier(attackingType, defenderTypes) helper usable by both team coverage and future features.

summary: This is an easy codebase to own: features map one-to-one onto route directories, all server/API knowledge sits behind a single query module of typed view models, and the framework usage (SolidStart 2 query + "use server", nitro() plugin in vite.config.ts) matches the current stable release. The recurring cost is duplication inside app/src/lib/server/pokeapi.ts — sprite URLs and type maps built two or three times, with homeList and teamDetails bypassing the existing card() helper. Route-page scaffolding is also copy-pasted across the four detail pages, which is what an Items section would feel most.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Delete the route directory, drop the 4-line getAbility wrapper, the abilityDetail function and its type, and the Abilities Section on the Pokémon page (the only inbound links). grep for 'abilities' confirms nothing else references it and there is no ability-specific CSS, so no dead code remains.

All card data is assembled server-side and PokemonCards just renders card.sprite, so no component changes — but the sprite URL is constructed in three functions (card():114, homeList():185, teamDetails():341), so one fix only covers every list if you fix all three or first refactor homeList/teamDetails to use the card() helper. All sites are in one file and findable via 'sprites/pokemon'.
